triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100) risks the '8. `cache_modifier` and `eviction_policy` are orthogonal levers with strict conditions' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100): 8. `cache_modifier` and `eviction_policy` are orthogonal levers with strict conditions

problem.statement: sm_100 Triton sparse-decode / split-K pitfalls -- 8. `cache_modifier` and `eviction_policy` are orthogonal levers with strict conditions

payload.attempted: Treat `.cg` / eviction hints as global "make memory faster" switches.
payload.lesson: Apply cache/eviction hints **per-load, per-kernel**, never globally. `evict_first` needs *(a)* the line is read exactly once over the kernel lifetime

established_fact.mechanism: `cache_modifier=".cg"` controls L1 bypass; `eviction_policy` is an L2 replacement hint — independent axes. Their value is entirely regime-dependent (grid fullness, re-touch pattern, freed-capacity size).

payload.observed: `.cg` on K loads **won** on an SM-starved split kernel (L1 can catch re-touched lines) but **regressed** the same loads on a fuller small-T grid (L1 is pure overhead when each CTA sees fresh K). `evict_first` on a re-read tensor cost **+3-4%** (hint evicted lines the loop re-reads → HBM refetch). And on **stores**, `.cg` + `evict_last` is a **ptxas error** ("`.evict_last` cannot be combined with `.cg`") — store-side L2 eviction is HW-LRU only on Blackwell.
payload.root_cause: `cache_modifier=".cg"` controls L1 bypass; `eviction_policy` is an L2 replacement hint — independent axes. Their value is entirely regime-dependent (grid fullness, re-touch pattern, freed-capacity size).
